title: Analytical Geometry: Distance, Midpoint and Gradient
seo_title: Grade 10 Analytical Geometry Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Represent geometric figures on a Cartesian co-ordinate system; derive and apply for any two points (x₁; y₁) and (x₂; y₂) a formula for calculating the distance between the two points, the gradient of the line segment joining the points, conditions for parallel and perpendicular lines, and the co-ordinates of the mid-point of the line segment.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 analytical geometry worksheets: distance formula, midpoint, gradient, and parallel and perpendicular lines. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Distance: AB = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²].
  • Midpoint: M = (x₁ + x₂2; y₁ + y₂2).
  • Gradient: m = y₂ − y₁x₂ − x₁.
  • Parallel lines: equal gradients. Perpendicular lines: m₁ × m₂ = −1.

Examples

Example

A(1; 2) and B(7; 10)

AB = √(36 + 64)

Answer: AB = 10, M(4; 6)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not squaringSquare both differences.
SubtractingThe midpoint adds.
Perpendicularm₁ × m₂ = −1.

items.q: What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to y = 3x − 8?
items.e: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: flip 3 and change the sign. −13. Check: 3 × (−13) = −1.

items.q: What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to y = 32x + 2?
items.e: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: flip 32 and change the sign. −23. Check: 32 × (−23) = −1.

items.q: What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to y = 23x + 3?
items.e: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals: flip 23 and change the sign. −32. Check: 23 × (−32) = −1.

items.q: What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to y = −2x − 4?

items.q: What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to y = 52x + 2?

items.q: A line passes through (−6; −2) and (−9; 0). What is the gradient of a line parallel to it?
items.e: Gradient = (0 − (−2)) ÷ (−9 − (−6)) = −23. Parallel lines have the same gradient: −23.

items.q: A line passes through (5; 6) and (9; 8). What is the gradient of a line parallel to it?
items.e: Gradient = (8 − 6) ÷ (9 − 5) = 12. Parallel lines have the same gradient: 12.

items.q: Write an equation of the line that passes through (−6; 4) and is parallel to 3x + y = 3.
items.e: A parallel line has the same gradient, −3. Substitute the point: 4 = −3(−6) + b, so b = −14. y = −3x − 14.

c: y = −25x − 35
items.e: A parallel line has the same gradient, 52. Substitute the point: −3 = 52(6) + b, so b = −18. y = 52x − 18.

items.q: Write an equation of the line that passes through (−6; 5) and is parallel to y = 32x + 1.

c: y = 34x + 72
y = −34x − 112
items.e: The given gradient is 34, so the perpendicular gradient is −43. Substitute the point: −1 = −43(−6) + b, so b = −9. y = −43x − 9.

items.q: Write an equation of the line that passes through (−2; −4) and is perpendicular to y = −12x − 5.
items.e: The given gradient is −12, so the perpendicular gradient is 2. Substitute the point: −4 = 2(−2) + b, so b = 0. y = 2x.

items.q: Write an equation of the line that passes through (−6; −6) and is perpendicular to 3x − y = −5.
items.e: The given gradient is 3, so the perpendicular gradient is −13. Substitute the point: −6 = −13(−6) + b, so b = −8. y = −13x − 8.

items.q: Write an equation of the line that passes through (4; 3) and is perpendicular to 2x + y = 3.
items.e: The given gradient is −2, so the perpendicular gradient is 12. Substitute the point: 3 = 12(4) + b, so b = 1. y = 12x + 1.

items.q: Write an equation of the line that passes through (6; −3) and is perpendicular to 2x − y = 2.
items.e: The given gradient is 2, so the perpendicular gradient is −12. Substitute the point: −3 = −12(6) + b, so b = 0. y = −12x.

items.q: Write an equation of the line that passes through (−6; 1) and is perpendicular to y = 3x.
items.e: The given gradient is 3, so the perpendicular gradient is −13. Substitute the point: 1 = −13(−6) + b, so b = −1. y = −13x − 1.

items.q: Are these lines parallel, perpendicular, or neither? y = −12x + 3 and 2x − y = 5
items.e: Solve the second equation for y: y = 2x − 5. Slopes: −12 and 2. The slopes multiply to −1, so the lines are perpendicular.

items.q: Are these lines parallel, perpendicular, or neither? y = 32x + 6 and y = 32x + 8
items.e: Slopes: 32 and 32. The slopes are equal (and the intercepts differ), so the lines are parallel.

items.q: Are these lines parallel, perpendicular, or neither? y = 3x − 3 and x + 3y = 0
items.e: Solve the second equation for y: y = −13x. Slopes: 3 and −13. The slopes multiply to −1, so the lines are perpendicular.

items.q: Are these lines parallel, perpendicular, or neither? y = −45x − 1 and 4x + 5y = 15
items.e: Solve the second equation for y: y = −45x + 3. Slopes: −45 and −45. The slopes are equal (and the intercepts differ), so the lines are parallel.

items.q: Are these lines parallel, perpendicular, or neither? y = 5x + 3 and y = 5x − 2
items.e: Slopes: 5 and 5. The slopes are equal (and the intercepts differ), so the lines are parallel.

items.q: Are these lines parallel, perpendicular, or neither? y = 23x − 4 and 2x + 3y = 3
items.e: Solve the second equation for y: y = −23x + 1. Slopes: 23 and −23. The slopes are not equal and do not multiply to −1, so the answer is neither. Opposite slopes are not enough; the numbers must also be flipped.

items.q: Rectangle ABCD has vertices A(1; 0), B(5; 0), C(5; 5), D(1; 5). Find its perimeter.
items.e: AB = 4 and BC = 5 (count or subtract coordinates). Perimeter = 2(4 + 5) = 18 units.

items.q: Find the area of triangle PQR with P(−6; −4), Q(2; −4) and R(1; −2).
items.e: Base PQ is horizontal: 8 units. Height is the vertical distance from R to the base: 2 units. Area = ½ × 8 × 2 = 8 square units.

items.q: Find the area of triangle PQR with P(−1; −3), Q(4; −3) and R(1; 2).
items.e: Base PQ is horizontal: 5 units. Height is the vertical distance from R to the base: 5 units. Area = ½ × 5 × 5 = 12,5 square units.

items.q: Rectangle ABCD has vertices A(−1; −3), B(6; −3), C(6; −1), D(−1; −1). Find its perimeter.
items.e: AB = 7 and BC = 2 (count or subtract coordinates). Perimeter = 2(7 + 2) = 18 units.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(0; −1), B(6; −1) and C(0; 7). Find its perimeter.
items.e: AB = 6, AC = 8. BC = √(6² + 8²) = 10 by the distance formula. Perimeter = 6 + 8 + 10 = 24 units.

items.q: P(0; −4), A(2; −2) and B(−2; −2) are the vertices of a triangle. Which statement is true?
c: AB² + PA² = PB², so angle PAB = 90°
PA² + PB² = AB², so angle APB = 90°
PA = PB = AB, so the triangle is equilateral
items.e: PA² = 8, PB² = 8 and AB² = 16. 8 + 8 = 16, so by the converse of Pythagoras' theorem angle APB = 90°.
